api:
<Dendrogram data={animals} name={|a: &Animal| a.name} features={|a: &Animal| a.traits.as_slice()} clusters={3} />
PropTypeDefault
dataas above: one row per leafrequired
nameFn(&T) -> &strrequired
featuresFn(&T) -> &[f64]: the values compared between rowsrequired
linkageLinkage::Single, Complete, Average or WardAverage
clustersusize: cut the tree into this many coloured clusters1
horizontalbool: leaves down the sidefalse
colorcolour, when clusters is 1the first series colour
value_axisAxisConfig for the merge distancefrom 0, labelled "Distance"
classTailwind classes ("h-64")

Rows are clustered by Euclidean distance, joining the two closest clusters again and again (the Lance–Williams method). The height of each join is the distance between the two clusters. Leaves are ordered so branches never cross. Links above the cut are drawn in the neutral colour.

examples.title: Three clusters
examples.description: Average linkage on speed, size, sociability and diet; the tree is cut into three coloured clusters.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn animal_tree() {
    let data = use_signal(animals());
    rsx! { <Dendrogram data={data} name={|a: &Animal| a.name} features={|a: &Animal| a.traits.as_slice()} clusters={3} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Countries
examples.description: Income, life expectancy and schooling grouped by Ward linkage.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn countries() {
    let data = use_signal(items(&[
        ("Norway", &[82., 83., 18.]),
        ("Germany", &[56., 81., 17.]),
        ("Japan", &[40., 84., 15.]),
        ("Brazil", &[9., 76., 8.]),
        ("Mexico", &[11., 75., 9.]),
        ("Turkey", &[10., 78., 8.]),
        ("India", &[2., 70., 7.]),
        ("Kenya", &[2., 67., 7.]),
        ("Nigeria", &[2., 55., 7.]),
        ("Canada", &[52., 82., 17.]),
    ]));
    rsx! { <Dendrogram data={data} name={|i: &Item| i.name} features={|i: &Item| i.values.as_slice()} linkage={Linkage::Ward} clusters={3} horizontal={true} class="h-96" /> }
}
